newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronic firms hit by power outage.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronic firms hit by power outage.

text.p: Several leading Taiwan electronic shares fell at mid-session on Tuesday after a 20-minute power outage in Taiwan's Hsinchu Science-based Industrial Park on Monday shut down their operations, brokers said.

With 70 minutes of trading left on Taipei's stock exchange, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co was down 50 cents, or 0.52 percent, to T$95.5, while United Microelectronics, fell T$1, or 1.5 percent, to T$66. Both shares traded actively.
The two leading chipmakers were among some 300 firms affected by the outage, science park officials said.
Figures for the exact amount of damage were not available, but some manufacturers estimated losses would total around T$1 billion.
But brokers said the impact would be short-lived.
"The reaction will only be short-term. It's not going to hurt electronics' sound fundamentals," said Chen Han-chung, a manager of Yungli Securities.
